card.name: Beni Ngoma
card.tagline: Colonial-era East African dance mimicking military brass bands
card.profile: Beni (also Mbeni or beni ngoma) is a competitive dance-society tradition of coastal and eastern Africa in which African performers in tunics and medals imitated European colonial military brass bands and drill, complete with officer hierarchies bearing European titles (Wikipedia: Beni (music); Ranger 1975). Originating in Swahili Mombasa in the 1890s, it spread inland through Tanganyika, Kenya, Nyasaland (Malawi), Zambia and Mozambique over some sixty years, spawning variant forms such as Mganda, Kalela and Malipenga (Ranger, Dance and Society in Eastern Africa, 1975).
card.insight: Filed here under Malawi but fundamentally pan-East-African; in Malawi the closely related military-mimicry dance is Malipenga (with mimed 'singing horns'), developed by King's African Rifles ex-servicemen after WWI (Wikipedia: Malipenga; SDNP Malawi).
